holisticNarrative.summary:
The GEHRIMED artifacts are stronger than many EHI export disclosures because they publish a large table-level dictionary with concrete column types and lengths rather than only high-level feature claims. Clinical domains are well represented across encounters, diagnoses/problems, medications/allergies, immunizations, labs, imaging-related content, schedules, and document/attachment storage. This supports real migration planning and indicates the export is not merely a USCDI summary projection.

The biggest practical migration challenge is not missing structure in general, but ambiguity in relational and semantic details. The glossary gives useful conventions (`Id`, `PatientID`, `DictationID`), yet there is no explicit FK/cardinality map or value-set binding table for many coded fields. Some domains also rely on generic payload columns (`data`, `addlData`), which increases interpretation risk without sample rows.

Using the EHI designated-record-set lens, the key substantive concern is financial completeness: documented billing indicators exist (CPT and charged flags), but dedicated claims/payment/remittance lifecycle structures are not clearly visible in the published schema. That could be a genuine designated-record-set gap if those data are stored in-product. By contrast, absence of dedicated security audit-log exports should not be treated as an EHI completeness failure.
standoutObservations: Strong: broad native table model disclosure (36 documented entities, typed columns) rather than only standards-mapped summaries.
Risky: relationship and value-set semantics are under-specified for robust automated reconstruction.
High impact: payment/remittance lifecycle is not clearly represented despite billing-related feature context.

Document/attachment structures include binary-capable fields (`Document.Doc` varbinary and `Attachments.ActualFile` image).
